story.title: Gloria Steinem, Influential Feminist Leader, Passes Away at 92
story.summary: Gloria Steinem, a prominent feminist activist, journalist, and co-founder of Ms. Magazine, has died at the age of 92. Her foundation announced that she passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by loved ones. Steinem was a significant figure in the women's rights movement, advocating for gender equality and social justice throughout her life.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Steinem’s death matter beyond one life?
explore_lenses.title: A legacy built into institutions
explore_lenses.summary: Steinem’s influence extended beyond celebrity: she helped create organizations and media outlets that continue to shape feminist advocacy and public debate.

claims.text: Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine, the National Women’s Political Caucus, the Ms. Foundation for Women and the Women’s Media Center, among other groups.
Ms. says its early reporting brought subjects including abortion rights, the Equal Rights Amendment, domestic violence, sexual harassment and date rape into national magazine coverage.

Jill Biden characterized Steinem’s work as a decades-long effort to secure women’s freedom to make decisions about their bodies, health and futures; this is Biden’s perspective, not a measure of policy outcomes.

explore_lenses.label: How did she turn journalism into activism?
explore_lenses.title: A magazine made movement issues public
explore_lenses.summary: Steinem used reporting, publishing and face-to-face organizing to connect feminist arguments with a broad national audience.

claims.text: Ms.’ preview issue sold out 300,000 test copies in eight days and generated 26,000 subscription orders and more than 20,000 reader letters within weeks, according to the magazine’s history.

The magazine’s history says Ms. faced advertiser resistance and financial instability, later adopting an advertising-free model before the Feminist Majority Foundation became its sole owner on December 31, 2001.

Steinem wrote that advertising still did not support the full range of women’s interests, despite women purchasing products such as books, wine, cars and insurance; this is her documented critique of the media market.
AP reported that Steinem spent much of her advocacy career speaking at campuses, community centers, rallies and marches, alongside her work as a writer and editor.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for her work and record?
explore_lenses.title: Institutions continue; memoir is scheduled
explore_lenses.summary: Her affiliated organizations and publications remain active, while a final memoir is scheduled for release later this month.

claims.text: Ms. remains published by the Feminist Majority Foundation and describes itself as a platform for feminist reporting, political analysis and engagement by new generations of writers and readers.
Random House has scheduled Steinem’s memoir, An Unexpected Life, for September 22, 2026, in hardcover, ebook and audiobook formats.

The publisher says the memoir addresses Steinem’s early life, formative political experiences, and progress and setbacks across more than six decades of activism; that is the publisher’s description of the forthcoming book.

story_report.summary: Gloria Steinem, the feminist activist, journalist and co-founder of Ms. magazine, has died at 92. A leading figure in the feminist movement for more than five decades, she combined writing and editing with public advocacy at campuses, community centers, rallies and marches. Her death closes a long public career devoted to women’s rights and leaves organizations and a magazine that continue to carry forward feminist reporting, political analysis and engagement.

sections.heading: Gloria Steinem’s Organizational Legacy
sections.body: Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine, the National Women’s Political Caucus, the Ms. Foundation for Women and the Women’s Media Center. Through its early reporting, Ms. said it brought abortion rights, the Equal Rights Amendment, domestic violence, sexual harassment and date rape into national magazine coverage. Jill Biden has characterized Steinem’s work as a decades-long effort to advance women’s freedom to make decisions about their bodies, health and futures.

sections.heading: Ms. Magazine’s Audience and Struggles
sections.body: According to the magazine’s history, Ms.’ preview issue sold out 300,000 test copies in eight days, prompting 26,000 subscription orders and more than 20,000 reader letters within weeks. The publication also faced advertiser resistance and financial instability, later adopting an advertising-free model before the Feminist Majority Foundation became sole owner on Dec. 31, 2001. Steinem argued that advertising did not support the full range of women’s interests, despite women’s purchasing power across major consumer categories.

sections.heading: Gloria Steinem’s Forthcoming Memoir
sections.body: Random House has scheduled Steinem’s memoir, An Unexpected Life, for publication on Sept. 22, 2026, in hardcover, ebook and audiobook editions. The publisher says the book will address her early life, formative political experiences, and progress and setbacks across more than six decades of activism. Ms. magazine remains published by the Feminist Majority Foundation.

related_stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated there is currently no need for additional mobilization in the Ukraine war, labeling such reports as Ukrainian disinformation. Additionally, Putin expressed optimism about the possibility of reaching a peace agreement, while Kyiv noted it anticipates a 'new dynamic' in peace efforts.

related_stories.title: Maltese Tycoon Acquitted in Journalist Murder Case, Activist Expresses Devastation
related_stories.summary: A Maltese tycoon has been acquitted of orchestrating the murder of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, who was killed by a car bomb in 2017. Tom Gibson, Deputy Director for the Committee to Protect Journalists, expressed his devastation over the not guilty verdict, highlighting the ongoing struggle for justice in cases involving attacks on journalists.

related_stories.title: Leon Black Sues House Committee After Skipping Epstein Deposition
related_stories.summary: Leon Black, a billionaire and former associate of Jeffrey Epstein, did not attend a scheduled deposition before the House Oversight Committee. Instead, he filed a lawsuit against the committee, seeking to block subpoenas related to its investigation into Epstein. Black had previously been subpoenaed in June after leaving a voluntary appearance abruptly.
